simulator_description: This simulator models COVID spread using a discrete-time stochastic SIR process over a fixed population N, tracking integer counts of Susceptible (S), Infected (I), and Recovered (R) at each time step. Transitions are sampled with binomial draws: new infections depend on an exponential force-of-infection 1-exp(-beta*I/N) applied to S, and new recoveries are Binomial(I, gamma), which is a sensible approximation to continuous-time SIR in daily steps while preserving randomness. The implementation enforces nonnegativity and exact conservation S+I+R=N after every step, aligning with the dataset assumption of constant population. Parameters (beta, gamma) are calibrated using only the specified observed trajectory (train id 0) by simulating many candidate trajectories and fitting a small neural conditional diagonal-Gaussian posterior estimator over bounded parameters, then generating posterior-predictive mean trajectories by averaging multiple stochastic rollouts (optionally across posterior samples) for each train/val/test agent to support MSE-based evaluation.
